title: Karl Marx — German Originals: The Manifest Witness Pair (1848 London / 1850-51 Cologne) and Das Kapital Erstauflage 1867 (secured, transcription queued)

manifest-1848.edition: Manifest der Kommunistischen Partei. [Anonymous.] London: Office der 'Bildungs-Gesellschaft fuer Arbeiter', Februar 1848. 23-page first printing.
manifest-1848.text_source: de.wikisource.org scan-backed transcription, BEARBEITUNGSSTAND=fertig (twice proofread), per-page revision-pinned (original/wikitext/ + wikisource-revision-pins.json)
manifest-1848.ref_scheme: manifest-1848 p<N> = page of the 1848 printing

manifest-1850-51.edition: 30-page printing long taken for the second London 1848 issue; per Meiser (MEGA-Studien 1996/1) printed ca. 1850/51 by J. Creteux at H. Becker's press, Cologne, reusing the London imprint, with Marx's express consent. Seated AS the Cologne witness under its true date.
manifest-1850-51.text_source: de.wikisource.org scan-backed transcription, fertig, per-page revision-pinned
manifest-1850-51.ref_scheme: manifest-1850-51 p<N> = page of the Cologne printing

kapital-1867.edition: Das Kapital. Kritik der politischen Oekonomie. Erster Band. Hamburg: Otto Meissner; New-York: L.W. Schmidt, 1867. ERSTAUFLAGE — the pre-revision Wertform text.

license.payload: All witness texts public domain (Marx d. 1883, Engels d. 1895; printings 1848-1867). Wikisource transcription layer CC BY-SA 4.0 (de.wikisource Editionsrichtlinien); Commons scan files PD. IA-hosted 1867 scans PD.
license.exclusions: MEW (Dietz) and MEGA apparatus texts excluded — edited-text copyright hazard. marxists.org German Kapital excluded as MEW-derived. Recorded 2026-08-22.

witness_program_note: First seat executed explicitly as a witness PAIR: the 1848 London and 1850/51 Cologne printings of the same work, page-addressed per witness so collation can locate the settings' divergences. The Cologne printing's false London imprint — a deliberate provenance mask, applied with the author's consent, uncovered by MEGA philology 145 years later — is itself a canonical object for the archive: provenance inversion in the wild, 1851.
normalization: Per-page flat lines '<witness> p<N>\t<text>', graphic flow per Wikisource transcription (Schreibweise folgt dem Originaltext), proofread headers and citation footers stripped. 23 + 29 content pages emitted (title/blank pages excluded by transcription).
